title: Capture from anywhere with a global shortcut
summary: Ctrl+Alt+C starts region capture from another application, including when ClipCraft is minimized, with visible conflict status and a session toggle.

Added: Global Ctrl+Alt+C while ClipCraft is running. Windows registration is event-driven and released when the instance closes or the shortcut is disabled.
Help > ClipCraft controls / About shows registration status and a session toggle. A conflicting application or second ClipCraft instance receives an explanation and retains toolbar capture.
Fixed: A global capture request wakes a minimized editor before starting selection.
Shortcuts during an active draft, dialog, gesture or capture are discarded instead of replaying later. Unsaved images keep the normal replacement confirmation.
Verified: Native activation from the synthetic fixture, minimized capture and all 256000 captured pixels through clipboard/import/save/reopen.
Changed New Image draft preservation, unsaved Cancel, repeated capture suppression, conflict reporting, disabling registration and successful retry in a second instance.
A local Windows registration test verifies exclusive ownership and reacquisition after cleanup without sending input to other apps.

limitations: The shortcut is fixed at Ctrl+Alt+C and its toggle lasts for the current session. Custom keys, persistent preferences, tray behavior and launch-at-startup remain planned.
ClipCraft must be running in the interactive desktop. Elevated applications, locked sessions and alternate keyboard layouts are not yet qualified.
Region capture still needs mixed-DPI, cross-display-drag, HDR and hot-plug qualification. Window, scrolling and video capture are unfinished.

Native Save As inspection remains blocked. Blocking file dialogs suppress the global shortcut in code, but their end-to-end native shortcut interaction remains unverified. Full interface parity is incomplete.
